_README: Archetype mean vectors for the trait sampler (briefing section 5).
DATA, NOT CODE. Editable without a rebuild: the sampler reads this file through
archetypes.ts and nothing here is compiled. Values are z-scores on a population
with mean 0 and standard deviation 1, so +1.4 is 'high' and -1.4 is 'low'.
MEANS ARE NAMED, NOT POSITIONAL. Author each trait by name. A bare array of six
decimals is the one place an index-order mistake could enter this component by
hand, and it would produce plausible-looking output that is wrong in a way no
eye would catch.
'sketch' is the briefing section 5 latent sketch the vector was authored against.
Keep it beside the numbers: it is the only record of what they were aiming at.
'defining' lists the traits the sketch actually pins. It is load-bearing, not
documentation: the separation constraint (briefing section 4.3) compares two
archetypes on the union of their defining traits, and traits the sketch leaves
free are deliberately excluded so a pair cannot pass on the strength of numbers
nobody chose. quietLurker is 'low E, moderate elsewhere', so extraversion is the
only thing that defines it.
AFTER EDITING, RUN 'npm run verify:traits'. Every pair of archetypes must sit at
least archetypeSeparation apart on the union of their defining traits, and the
loader enforces it on startup. Two archetypes closer than that are one archetype
with two names.
'version' NAMES THIS SET. Quality bounds and calibration surfaces are properties of a
specific archetype set, not of the generator in the abstract: a legitimate improvement
here moves them. Any bound written against these numbers must name this version.
POSITIONS COME FROM A JOINT SOLVE, not from hand-placement. The fifteen
between-archetype correlations are coupled across the points, so fixing one pair moves
the others; sequential patching does not converge. Run 'npm run solve:archetypes' after
any edit, read the proposal as descriptions of people, and only then accept it.
PROVENANCE, DECLARED BEFORE THE REFERENCE COMPARISON RUNS AND NOT AFTER.
product-role         exists for a product reason and survives regardless of what
clustering real data says. Needs no empirical backing to be useful.
empirical-candidate  authored to sketch a personality space. Reference data may revise
or retire it.
Declared NOW because doing it afterwards lets a real finding be argued away ('that one
was always a product role') and lets a product decision be defended as empirical. The
split happens to match the pinned/free split used by solve:archetypes, and that is not a
coincidence: 'this position carries product meaning' and 'this archetype survives
whatever the data says' are the same question in different words.
BOTH MOMENTS OF THE z-SCORE CLAIM ARE NOW SOLVED FOR, not just the standard deviation.
The specification says population mean 0 AND sd 1; only the sd was ever constrained, and
the mean was measured at +0.213 on honesty once anyone looked. Worst mean is now 0.045.
Both are properties of (SET x MIX), not of the set alone: they are solved against the
DEFAULT equal mix, and a different archetypeMix reintroduces an offset in both.
THESE ARE PRE-STANDARDISATION COORDINATES (D-101). The sampler standardises its output
per trait, (x - mean) / sd, against the moments of whatever (set x mix) it is given, so
the z-score claim holds for ANY mix rather than for the one the set was solved against.
An avatar drawn from professionalSupport therefore does NOT sit at the mean written
here. Relative structure is untouched: every point shifts by the same constant and
scales by the same per-trait factor, so separation and semantics are preserved.
The solve's mean and sd targets remain, as a convenience rather than a requirement:
they keep the standardisation close to the identity at the default mix, which is what
keeps these numbers readable as the coordinates somebody actually authored.
SEPARATION IS CHECKED IN STANDARDISED SPACE, and it is mix-dependent: distances scale
by 1/sd per trait. The loader asserts the floor against the DEFAULT mix because it
cannot know a caller's; verify:traits sweeps several and prints the dependence.

archetypes.label: Average
archetypes.sketch: moderate throughout, slightly high E and N
archetypes.provenanceWhy: Anchors the centre of the space. A structural role; it is not a claim that "average person" is an empirical cluster.

archetypes.label: Role model
archetypes.sketch: low N, strongly high E, above average on everything else
archetypes.note: POSITION FROM THE JOINT SOLVE (npm run solve:archetypes), not hand-placed: the fifteen between-archetype correlations are coupled across the eleven points and cannot be satisfied one pair at a time. The label was checked against the solved position afterwards, not the other way round. RE-SOLVED under the MEAN constraint: the z-score claim has two halves and only the standard deviation was ever constrained, so the population mean sat at +0.213 on honesty. Constraining it moved honest weight downward across the set, which is the balance the constraint necessarily implies. SKETCH REVISED, NOT THE VECTOR. Briefing CCB-S4-003 §5 sketched this as 'low N, high on everything else'. After the mean constraint it sits at O 0.58, A 0.62 and H 0.70, which is above average rather than high. The label follows the position, so the sketch is corrected to what the vector now says rather than the check being relaxed to accept it. This is the cost the mean constraint was accepted with: for every honest archetype there has to be dishonest weight to balance it, and some of that balance came out of this one.
archetypes.provenanceWhy: Authored to sketch a personality space. Reference data is allowed to revise or retire this one.

archetypes.label: Ingratiator
archetypes.sketch: high C, high E, high A, low H; organised, warm, socially skilled, and self-serving with it
archetypes.note: AUTHORED, NOT SKETCHED IN THE BRIEFING, and product-driven rather than read off any data. It fills a quadrant the original eight left empty: every agreeable archetype in that set was also honest, so Honesty-Humility carried no variation independent of Agreeableness (r = 0.935 across the eight means) and the set could not express the good-faith versus manipulative distinction the sixth dimension exists to make. In a room this is the member who is pleasant to everyone and is working it. When reference data lands, whether real populations contain a type resembling this becomes an answerable question and the answer may revise it. POSITION FROM THE JOINT SOLVE (npm run solve:archetypes), not hand-placed: the fifteen between-archetype correlations are coupled across the eleven points and cannot be satisfied one pair at a time. The label was checked against the solved position afterwards, not the other way round. RE-SOLVED under the MEAN constraint: the z-score claim has two halves and only the standard deviation was ever constrained, so the population mean sat at +0.213 on honesty. Constraining it moved honest weight downward across the set, which is the balance the constraint necessarily implies.

archetypes.note: AUTHORED, NOT SKETCHED IN THE BRIEFING, and product-driven. Together the two make Honesty-Humility carry information Agreeableness does not, which is what the sixth dimension was added for. archetypes.label: Anxious and scrupulous
archetypes.sketch: high N, high H; the worrier who is meticulously fair
archetypes.note: AUTHORED, NOT SKETCHED IN THE BRIEFING, and product-driven. Added for COVERAGE rather than to reach a number: the joint solve satisfied the neuroticism/honesty correlation target by rebalancing the other archetypes and left this region empty, so the correlation was repaired while the population gap remained. Frets about doing the right thing, apologises more than necessary, entirely trustworthy. Its absence encoded the proposition that anxious people are less honest, which nothing supports and the model explicitly denies.
